welcome.title: Geofence Lab
welcome.body: Draw your company's perimeter and the rooms inside it. The app tells you when you enter and leave each one.

how.title: How it works
how.body: Two tiers, to spare the battery.
how.bullet1: The system watches nearby companies and wakes the app.
how.bullet2: Only then does the GPS start, to tell which room you are in.
how.bullet3: On the way out it stops. At rest, no position is requested.

onb-01.title: Welcome to Geofence Lab
onb-01.body: Register a place and draw its rooms to start tracking entries and exits.

onb-02.title: Location permission
onb-02.body: To work with the app closed, monitoring needs "always" access.

onb-03.title: Radius and active radius
onb-03.body: Entry is detected at the radius; the exit only past the active radius. The slack between them prevents repeated events.

onb-04.title: Rooms
onb-04.body: Inside a place, polygons bound each room and raise events of their own.

onb-05.title: Simulator
onb-05.body: Use the simulator to play a fake route and watch the events without leaving your chair.

d-1-1.title: Geofencing lives in the system
d-1-1.body: Region monitoring runs in the OS, not in the app — which is why it works with the app closed.

d-1-2.title: The region ceiling
d-1-2.body: iOS monitors 20 regions per app; Android, 100. A moving window covers all 500 places.

d-1-3.title: Guard region
d-1-3.body: One of the slots watches the set itself: leaving it is the signal that the window went stale.

d-1-4.title: Minimum radius
d-1-4.body: Circles under about 100 m do not fire reliably on iOS. That is why rooms use polygons.

d-1-5.title: Two tiers
d-1-5.body: The native region wakes the app; continuous GPS only turns on afterwards, while you are inside.

d-1-6.title: Battery
d-1-6.body: At rest the app asks for no position at all — the device's own radio does the waiting.

d-1-7.title: Persistence
d-1-7.body: State and events live in SQLite, the only storage you can trust inside a background task.

d-2-1.title: Accuracy matters
d-2-1.body: A reading with 300 m of error is not information: it is discarded before it can become an event.

d-2-2.title: Confidence margin
d-2-2.body: Entry is only declared once the whole error circle fits inside the radius.

d-2-3.title: Confirmations
d-2-3.body: A transition needs consecutive readings that agree — GPS noise does not turn into a notification.

d-2-4.title: Dwell time
d-2-4.body: A freshly assumed state is held for a few seconds before it can change again.

d-2-5.title: Ray casting
d-2-5.body: Telling whether a point sits in a room is counting how many edges a ray crosses: odd means inside.

d-2-6.title: Bounding box
d-2-6.body: Before testing the edges, four comparisons rule out whatever is plainly outside.

d-2-7.title: The boundary
d-2-7.body: A point exactly on the edge always counts as inside — the rule is explicit, not a coin toss.

d-3-1.title: No duplicates
d-3-1.body: Every transition carries a sequence number: repeating the same reading raises no second event.

d-3-2.title: Initial state on iOS
d-3-2.body: iOS reports the state of every region at each app start. Without the persisted key, everything would fire again.

d-3-3.title: Transaction
d-3-3.body: The new state and the event are written together, or neither of them is.

d-3-4.title: Offline is the normal case
d-3-4.body: The queue is the state: nothing is lost because a request failed.

d-3-5.title: Backoff
d-3-5.body: Each retry waits twice as long as the last, up to a ceiling — and gives up after a few.

d-3-6.title: Reconciliation
d-3-6.body: The scheduler compares the plan against what the OS holds, and corrects the difference.

d-3-7.title: Sliding window
d-3-7.body: Only the next notifications are handed to the OS, well under the iOS ceiling of 64.

d-4-1.title: Terminated app on Android
d-4-1.body: A killed app is not relaunched by a geofence event — hence the foreground service.

d-4-2.title: Terminated app on iOS
d-4-2.body: iOS relaunches the app to deliver a region event, with a few seconds of runtime.

d-4-3.title: Manufacturers
d-4-3.body: Battery managers from some manufacturers kill the service anyway.

d-4-4.title: Device reboot
d-4-4.body: Without a boot receiver, monitoring does not come back on its own after a restart.

d-4-5.title: Subtitle
d-4-5.body: The notification subtitle only exists on iOS; on Android it becomes the first line of the body.

d-4-6.title: Two-step permission
d-4-6.body: Background access can only be asked for once foreground access has been granted.

d-4-7.title: End of the series
d-4-7.body: You have walked through all four weeks. The event log keeps recording everything.

permissionBlocked.title: Notifications are blocked
permissionBlocked.body: The sequence is paused: the system is not allowing notifications from this app. Enable them in the device settings.
